tagline.text: The central town of Bantayan Island, with an old coral-stone church, a market and mangroves

location.label: Location
location.text: Western Bantayan Island, Cebu Province, in the Bantayan town proper

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to one day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–2,500 (per person, one day staying in Santa Fe)

children.text: Bantayan Town is the largest town on Bantayan Island, where you can see the coral-stone Church of Saints Peter and Paul, which began as a parish around 1580, along with the market and a mangrove boardwalk. It offers a different side of island life from the resorts of Santa Fe.

Bantayan (Bantayan Town) is the island's largest municipality, on the western side of Bantayan Island. Including its outlying islands it covers about 82 km², and with about 87,000 residents in 2024 it has the biggest population on the island. Of its 25 barangays, Bantigue, Binaobao, Suba and Ticad form the town center. It is about 136 km from Cebu City, and borders Madridejos to the north, Medellin to the east and Santa Fe to the south. Poultry farming has flourished so much that it is nicknamed the "Egg Basket of the Visayas."

The center of the town is the Church of Saints Peter and Paul. The parish is said to have been founded by the Augustinians on June 11, 1580, and is counted among the oldest parishes in the Visayas and Mindanao. The present church is the fifth on the same site; construction began in 1839 and took about 24 years, using coral stone. The stone walls carry relief carvings, and the belfry is said to overlook the sea.

Old houses and heritage remain here and there in town. Easy places to look around include Casa de Antiguedades, a private collection of antiques, the St. Helena Botanical Garden, and the Bantayan Nature Park created in 2012. Typhoon Yolanda in 2013 collapsed the Abello and del Rosario ancestral houses, and the D.C. Abello Theater, built in 1952, was demolished in early 2015. As a result, today's streets center on public buildings and the market.

For travelers, Bantayan Town is the place to see island daily life. Many lodgings are in Santa Fe, but banks, ATMs, the market and restaurants are concentrated in this town. A common route is to look around the church and plaza, eat at the market and walk to the Obo-ob Mangrove Eco Park, and it is also known as a place with beautiful sunsets. After the earthquake, the church and some public facilities may be closed for building safety checks, so do not rely on old information and confirm on site. A walk around the town center takes only 1–2 hours, which makes it a good fit for a half-day in the morning.

blocks.title: Church of Saints Peter and Paul

children.text: Its features are a heavy coral-stone exterior, stone reliefs and a belfry with a sea view. On the night of Good Friday during Holy Week, a procession of religious images winds along the plaza. The September 30, 2025 northern Cebu earthquake partly collapsed the front gable and restricted entry inside, so check the repair and opening status before you go. As of the parish's October 2025 statement the building stayed closed until deemed safe and Masses were held on the church grounds, and a December 2025 report said only that repairs were expected to start in 2026. The plaza in front of the church is lively from early morning with stalls and motorbikes, and the midday sun is strong, so it is better to look around in the morning.
The church belfry has a view over the sea, and a small museum is said to open by appointment. Ask the parish office whether it is open.

This is a mangrove forest park (OMAGIECA) in Obo-ob village, with a bamboo boardwalk of about 1 km through the forest and a viewing tower. Admission is about ₱50–75 depending on the guide. Some guides give about ₱20 for children and about ₱170 for kayaking. It is also known as a filming location for the movie Camp Sawi, and mornings are cool. Climbing the tower at the end of the bamboo boardwalk gives a view of forest and sea together, and guides say it is about 20–25 minutes by motorbike from Santa Fe.

Market eateries serve dishes such as fish tinola and, in season, baby shark adobo cheaply. Snacks such as puto balanghoy (a cassava cake), suman and cassava in syrup cost about ₱10–20. Danggit and dried squid are also sold at the market. The market is liveliest from dawn through the morning, and some stalls close in the afternoon, so it is better to go before lunch.

On Maundy Thursday and Good Friday, floats carrying religious images are carried on foot around town. Islanders and visitors from all over Cebu gather, and the mood is both solemn and noisy. Lodging is full months in advance during this period.

The Palawod Festival, held on June 29, the feast of Saints Peter and Paul, is the biggest in Bantayan Town. Street events and parades honoring fishing mix together. Dates and events change every year, so check the latest announcements.
At the end of January a Sinulog celebration runs for ten or more days. It is not as big as Cebu City's Sinulog, but the town plaza is busy.

The beaches at Sillon and Baigad on the Bantayan Town coast are mostly undeveloped, and some have debris washed up by the waves. Think of them as the shore of a local fishing community rather than a tourist beach.

There is no regular city bus on the island: trisikads (pedicabs) serve short distances, motor tricycles longer ones, and jeepneys board at the Santa Fe pier. The minimum tricycle fare is about
The church, plaza and market can all be reached on foot. There are also old houses around the plaza.
Obo-ob mangroves are about
15–20 minutes
by tricycle or motorbike.
Bantayan Town is best in the dry season,
December–May

. The sea is calm, motorbike travel is easy and the town's sunsets are clear. During Holy Week (late March to mid-April) you can see the processions, but the whole island is crowded and lodging prices rise two to three times. Repair schedules after the earthquake depend on local announcements, so confirm before you leave whether the church and facilities are open.
In the rainy season,
June–November
, showers are frequent, and especially in
September–November
typhoons can stop ferries. The June 29 Palawod Festival falls in the rainy season but is the town's biggest event, so if you plan around it, book lodging early.

Bantayan Town also has small lodgings and hostels, but traveler lodgings are mostly on the Santa Fe beaches. Banks and ATMs are in this town, so even if you stay in Santa Fe, withdraw cash here. According to guides, lodging prices rise two to three times during Holy Week.

Food is concentrated around the market and the plaza. Near the plaza there is a café selling Western pizza and coffee (Kermit's Café and Pastry) and a Filipino rice restaurant (Jala's Restaurant), and market eateries serve fish tinola and, in season, baby shark adobo cheaply. Puto balanghoy, suman and cassava in syrup are snacks at about ₱10–20, and at night people gather in the plaza, with restaurants and bars open.

Because it is where the most people on the island live, it is easy to get small change and daily necessities. Banks and ATMs are in town, and Globe, Smart and TM signals are available. Prices are lower than in tourist-heavy Santa Fe, so it is a good place to stock up on snacks and water.
The church is a place of worship, so avoid Mass times and look around quietly. Some areas have been closed since the earthquake.
Obo-ob mangroves are cool in the morning, and the hours differ by guide (6:00–18:00 or 8:00–17:00), so it is safer to go early.
At the market you can buy danggit and dried squid vacuum-packed. Compare prices between shops.
During Holy Week lodging and ferry tickets sell out months ahead, so book early.
ATMs are few on the island. Withdraw enough in Bantayan Town.
When renting a motorbike, check the rental terms, fuel level and helmet first.
For sunsets, the west side of the island, Bantayan Town and Madridejos, is best.

The September 30, 2025 northern Cebu earthquake collapsed part of the front of the Church of Saints Peter and Paul and damaged buildings and a school in Bantayan Town. Entry to the church may be restricted, so check before you go.
Reviewers say the cottages at the mangrove eco park were lost to a typhoon. Check the condition of facilities on site.
With little public transport on the island, plan your day around the last ferry. Leave a day's buffer before your flight home.
Old houses are privately owned. Do not enter without permission.
Some beaches have debris and are less developed. For swimming, the resort-managed beaches of Santa Fe are recommended.
In typhoon season the whole island is prone to wind damage. Check the forecast before you leave.
